answer: We formulate a mechanism combining dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices to ensure Sybil resistance. Agents harbor an incentive to participate truthfully, as multiplying identities incurs a strictly positive expected opportunity cost. The thread of strategic interactions reveals that, in equilibrium, agents opt for a single identity. Under sable conditions, the punishment matrix deters Sybil attacks, guaranteeing a strict Nash equilibrium wherein no agent benefits from deviating.
